topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I stood there, the world around me muted by the weight of his words. "I don't remember you," he said, and my heart, a fragile leaf, trembled in the gust of his forgetfulness. Years dissolved into seconds, each memory a vivid splash against the canvas of our forgotten friendship. I smiled, a thin, practiced curve, masking the storm within. How does one reconcile with a past that has been erased from another’s mind? It was a puzzle, an invisible chasm between us, and I reached out, fingers brushing the edges of a void. Yet, there was resolve in the silence, a quiet determination to weave new threads, to stitch our story anew, however tenuous the connection.
